title: Chapter 13 Quiz: Performance & Optimization
description: Test your knowledge of performance techniques, lazy loading, reactivity optimization, virtual scrolling, and profiling.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of code splitting in Vue?
options: To reduce the initial bundle size by loading parts of the app on demand
To make the app easier to debug
questions.explanation: Code splitting splits the bundle into chunks that are loaded only when needed, improving initial load time.

questions.question: The `defineAsyncComponent` function can accept a loading component and a timeout.
questions.explanation: Yes, you can pass an object with `loader`, `loadingComponent`, `errorComponent`, `delay`, and `timeout`.

questions.question: The Vue function used to create a lazy‑loaded async component is __________.
questions.explanation: `defineAsyncComponent` is the Vue 3 API for defining async components.

questions.question: `shallowReactive` makes all nested properties reactive as well.
questions.explanation: `shallowReactive` only tracks first‑level properties; deeper properties are not reactive.

questions.question: Which technique is best for rendering a list of 10,000 items?
options: Using a computed property to filter the list
questions.explanation: Virtual scrolling renders only the visible items, drastically reducing DOM nodes and improving performance.

questions.question: The performance metric that measures when the largest content element is rendered is __________.
questions.explanation: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) indicates when the main content has loaded.

questions.question: Computed properties are re‑evaluated on every render, regardless of dependency changes.
questions.explanation: Computed properties are cached and only re‑evaluate when their reactive dependencies change.

questions.question: Which Vue Devtools feature helps identify slow component renders?
questions.explanation: The Performance tab records and displays component render times in a flame graph.

questions.question: To mark an object as never to be made reactive, use __________.
questions.explanation: `markRaw` prevents an object from being converted to a proxy by Vue's reactivity system.

questions.question: Using `v-once` on static content can improve performance by skipping future updates.
questions.explanation: `v-once` renders the element once and never updates it, reducing reactivity overhead.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of memoization?
options: To make functions run faster by caching results
To make code easier to read
questions.explanation: Memoization caches the results of expensive function calls to avoid repeating work for the same inputs.

questions.question: The technique of rendering only the visible portion of a large list is called __________.
questions.explanation: Virtual scrolling renders only the items in the viewport, plus a buffer.

questions.question: The `v-memo` directive can be used to memoize a subtree based on dependency values.
questions.explanation: `v-memo` (Vue 3.2+) caches a template subtree and only re‑renders when dependencies change.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign of a performance bottleneck in a Vue app?
questions.explanation: High TBT indicates the main thread is busy for too long, often due to inefficient code or many updates.

questions.question: To see the bundle size and identify large dependencies, you can use the __________ tool.
questions.explanation: Webpack Bundle Analyzer visualizes the size of the output bundles.

questions.question: Lazy loading route components in Vue Router can significantly reduce the initial bundle size.
questions.explanation: By using dynamic imports for route components, you load them only when the route is visited.

questions.question: What does the `shallowRef` function do?
options: Creates a shallow reactive reference that tracks `.value` assignment but not deep mutations
Creates a reference that triggers updates on every property access
questions.explanation: `shallowRef` only triggers updates when the `.value` property is reassigned; nested properties are not reactive.

questions.question: The __________ tool in the browser's DevTools can record JavaScript execution and identify long tasks.
questions.explanation: The Performance tab records a timeline of browser activity, including JavaScript execution.

questions.question: Using a computed property that depends on many reactive values can cause performance issues if those values change frequently.
questions.explanation: If dependencies change often, the computed property will recompute frequently, which may be expensive.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good practice for improving initial load performance?
options: Use dynamic imports for non‑critical components
questions.explanation: Dynamic imports (lazy loading) for components that are not immediately needed reduces the initial bundle size.
